title: Does It Not Grief, and Wonder Move
description: Does It Not Grief, and Wonder Move in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book II, hymn 14, “Elijah's prayer. 1Ki 18”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Does it not grief, and won-der move, To think of Is-rael's shame-ful fall? Who need-ed mir-a-cles to prove Wheth-er the Lord was God, or Baal!

lines: Does it not grief, and wonder move,
To think of Israel's shameful fall?
Who needed miracles to prove
Whether the Lord was God, or Baal!
Methinks I see Elijah stand,
His features glow with love and zeal,
In faith and prayer he lifts his hand,
And makes to heav'n his great appeal,
"O God! if I thy servant am,
If 'tis thy message fills my heart;
Now glorify thy holy name,
And show this people who thou art!"
He spake, and lo! a sudden flame
Consumed the wood, the dust, the stone;
The people struck, at once proclaim
"The Lord is God, the Lord alone."
Like him we mourn an aweful day,
When more for Baal, than God appear;
Like him, believers, let us pray,
And may the God of Israel hear!
Lord, if thy servant speaks thy truth,
If he indeed is sent by thee;
Confirm the word to all our youth,
And let them thy salvation see.
Now may thy Spirit's holy fire
Pierce every heart that hears thy word;
Consume each hurtful vain desire,
And make them know thou art the Lord.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
